title: Marvelous Designer Discord Contests Are Back: Introducing the Marvelous Winter Market
content:
![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202512/c3ccfa2c78974a988e8f2ea56ecd5fde/images/81e29614506f4313b361ad928835f1abMarvelous%20Winter%20Market%20%281%29.png)  
![9920b9e62c294de4888adf8a479495d7](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202512/c3ccfa2c78974a988e8f2ea56ecd5fde/images/9920b9e62c294de4888adf8a479495d7Marvelous%20Winter%20Market%20%281%29.png)

We’re excited to bring back Marvelous Designer Discord contests with a brand-new creative challenge: ❄️Marvelous Winter Market❄️

Design winter market looks and scenes. You can focus on characters and their garments (vendor, guard, performer, shoppers) and/or environments (stalls, tents, signs, bags). The finished artwork can range from one highly detailed 3D model, to a scene in a shop, to a bird’s eye view of a bustling market. Be creative with your interpretation of “winter market”. It doesn’t need to be holiday themed, but it can be.

**Prizes**

🥇 First Place: 12 months of FREE Marvelous Designer and a feature on our social media  
🥈 Second Place: 6 months of FREE Marvelous Designer  
🥉 Third Place: 3 months of FREE Marvelous Designer

**Dates**

Begin creating now! Submissions will open January 16th and close January 30th.

**How To Enter**

To enter, just join the official Marvelous Designer Discord server. Come for the contest, stay for the community!

  
[**[Join the official Marvelous Designer Discord Server]**](https://discord.com/invite/pPEmF86DHc)
content_description: Join the Marvelous Designer Discord for the exciting Marvelous Winter Market contest, where you can showcase your creativity by designing unique winter market looks and scenes for a chance to win fantastic prizes!

title: Adobe Substance 3D
content:
Hello.

Unreal Engine 5.7 came out on November 12, 2025, and the LiveSync plugin was updated reasonably soon after. Unfortunately, over a month later, I get an error when I attempt to use it because Substance has not been updated by Adobe. Is there a way for me to bypass having to use Substance for my materials? 

Thanks.

### Community Post Comments:
Comment 1: Thank you for responding, Bryan. It’s been three weeks since I posted this, and I’ve been working on other things while I waited, but I opened the relevant project just now to confirm what you are telling me. The “error” message is still there, but I see now it says, “...otherwise default materials will be applied to garments.” My understanding, based on the official instructions, “Setting up Unreal Engine & LiveSync,” is that Substance is/was required. The very first bullet point, which states: “1. Install Substance 3D for Unreal Engine plugin for a desired Unreal Engine version,” and the fourth bullet point, “4. Make sure that LiveSync and Substance 3D for Unreal Engine plugin are enabled in Plugins settings” led me to believe so. Would you mind telling me what is the difference between Substance materials and “default” materials? Again, thank you.

Comment 2: Hi Melissa,The latest version of the LiveSync plugin is designed to function independently of the Substance 3D plugin. Consequently, the resulting assets will be standard Material Assets rather than Substance materials within Unreal Engine.I tested this using CLO 2025.2, Unreal Engine 5.7, and LiveSync 2.2.1 and was unable to replicate the error. Could you provide more details regarding the specific issue you are experiencing?Best regards,Bryan

Comment 3: It's now been over six weeks and Adobe still hasn't updated the Substance plugin...
content_description: This webpage aims to provide solutions for bypassing Substance in Unreal Engine 5.7 due to compatibility issues following recent updates.

title: Behind the Scenes of ‘Mirage’: Capturing the Desert Wind
content:
## _Where cinematic atmosphere meets intricate costume detail. Discover how artists_[ _Hyun-jong Kim_](https://www.behance.net/Kinn_hj) _and_[ _Min-ji Oh_](https://www.artstation.com/ohminji3) _brought inspiration from Dune to life using Marvelous Designer, revealing their collaborative workflow and secrets to achieving hyper-realistic cloth simulation._

YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Ax346ZAUXUo

# **Could you introduce yourselves?**

**Hyun-jong Kim :**  
Hello, I am Kim Hyun-jong, a 3D artist. I mainly work with Cinema 4D and Blender. Over the past two years, I have focused on learning Marvelous Designer and actively applying it to my personal projects. I enjoy creating cinematic visuals, so I have conducted various projects centered around that style.

I have been working as a 3D artist for about five years. During this time, my work has been well-received, winning awards in various categories at the Rookies Awards, LACA, and the Motion Design Awards. These experiences have served as a strong foundation for refining the direction and quality of my work.

![d2f02cb1dc3349ac985bcdf8c2ccbc89](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202512/80d4961da95048638f075d52a4b7af6b/images/d2f02cb1dc3349ac985bcdf8c2ccbc89Eyes_of_Empire_Behind_3_GIF-ezgif.com-resize%20%281%29.gif)![1223dde8d89a41899c11032b00c9e08c](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202512/80d4961da95048638f075d52a4b7af6b/images/1223dde8d89a41899c11032b00c9e08cEyes_of_Empire_thumbnail_1.png)

**Min-ji Oh:**  
I am Oh Min-ji, currently working as a 3D Asset Artist at 2grey. I started learning CG in earnest in 2018 to prepare for my career, and it has been about four years since I entered the industry. Originally, I aimed to be a generalist and experienced various parts of CG, but I felt particularly excited and enthusiastic whenever I worked on character modeling. I think that is why I naturally ended up pursuing the path of a modeler.

I often use costumes as a key element to express a character's personality, and Marvelous Designer has been an indispensable tool in that process. As I continued working with Marvelous Designer from the beginning of my studies until now, my skills naturally improved, which led to the opportunity to join Hyun-jong's project.

![65062147414144d4a39876c97dbf2486](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202512/80d4961da95048638f075d52a4b7af6b/images/65062147414144d4a39876c97dbf2486Flea_Render_2.jpg)

# **Let’s discuss your recent project, ‘Mirage,’ created using Marvelous Designer. Where did you find inspiration for the concept, and what visual style were you aiming for?**

![e74db7dabce54cbeb91c304dd50f92f0](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202512/80d4961da95048638f075d52a4b7af6b/images/e74db7dabce54cbeb91c304dd50f92f0imgi_91_30892a232584561.68aefd17067b4.png)

The inspiration for creating 'Mirage' came after watching the movies _Dune_ and _Lawrence of Arabia_. I was deeply inspired by the restrained depiction of vast deserts in both films and wanted to create a piece based on that motif.

The overall narrative centers on the story of T.E. Lawrence dispatched to the Middle East during World War I, while the visual style was largely developed by drawing reference from _Dune_. For the costume design, I referenced traditional Bedouin attire to capture the Middle Eastern atmosphere, placing special emphasis on expressing the movement of the fabric fluttering in the wind.

# **How did you utilize Marvelous Designer for this project? I’m also curious about the brief pipeline regarding how you integrated it with other tools.**

First, for character animation, we used data based on an AI motion capture tool where I acted out the necessary actions myself. For additional movements, we utilized Mixamo preset animations. Facial animation was created using the 'Move by Maxon' application. Afterwards, any awkward or jittery parts of the mocap data were polished using keyframe animation to ensure smooth movement.

![f9e74bf30d6142c5a6dd3ac211ee4eb9](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202512/80d4961da95048638f075d52a4b7af6b/images/f9e74bf30d6142c5a6dd3ac211ee4eb9Mirage_thumbnail_2.png)

Once the animation was complete, we exported it as Alembic data to ensure stability during simulation and prepared to dress the character in Marvelous Designer.

In the costume production phase, we focused our plan specifically on the detailed movements of the main character's turban and scarf. Since the entire outfit required simulation in the video, we determined the workflow by anticipating potential issues beforehand. With the turban, scarf, and clothing all needing to collide, simulating the turban itself proved to be quite unstable.

![524deca99d4b4c8fabb4682c2845b4d7](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202512/80d4961da95048638f075d52a4b7af6b/images/524deca99d4b4c8fabb4682c2845b4d7Mirage_Behind_1.png)

Therefore, we shaped the turban's natural wrinkles and form in Marvelous Designer first, but handled it through rigging rather than simulation. This allowed us to add significant details and extra wrinkles in ZBrush later.

![d026a72210134411b90a1799e6c45daf](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202512/80d4961da95048638f075d52a4b7af6b/images/d026a72210134411b90a1799e6c45dafimgi_411_d85329232584561.68b2ded6aa157.gif)![cccc0c4db08f472eaab0993f6b9735b2](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202512/80d4961da95048638f075d52a4b7af6b/images/cccc0c4db08f472eaab0993f6b9735b2imgi_492_f70e17232584561.68b06a2fc4cff-ezgif.com-resize.gif)

For the scarf, it needed to flutter in the wind and exhibit many wrinkles due to the material's nature. We adjusted the particle distance to a low value and frequently checked the physical properties by applying wind during the process. We didn't create the fluttering section as a single pattern; instead, we split it into two pieces to prevent the pattern from becoming unnecessarily large.

Typically, after the Marvelous Designer stage, we import the model into ZBrush to add details like seams and fine wrinkles, and then to Substance Painter for additional weathering. However, since the base form needs realistic wrinkles, we spend considerable time in Marvelous Designer tweaking various properties until the wrinkles look authentic. For simulation optimization, we didn't perform separate retopology but instead adjusted the mesh style settings directly within Marvelous Designer.

![d7cff6e94ad047728d273349fe7eacb5](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202512/80d4961da95048638f075d52a4b7af6b/images/d7cff6e94ad047728d273349fe7eacb5Mirage_Behind_2.png)

Regarding the simulation, the most critical element in the full-body shots was the form of the scarf fluttering in the wind. To achieve this, we conducted numerous tests, finely adjusting the physical property values set during the production phase. As a result, we set the military uniform to a relatively thick fabric, making it slightly heavier than the default properties, while the scarf was set to be thinner and lighter to create a clear distinction. This allowed the scarf’s movement to stand out even under the same wind intensity, enabling us to achieve the desired visual satisfactorily.

![85d9a2a2b8de4abfa410cb113a3b531a](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202512/80d4961da95048638f075d52a4b7af6b/images/85d9a2a2b8de4abfa410cb113a3b531aimgi_486_14123d232584561.68adc02a415c9-ezgif.com-resize.gif)

For specific shots, we also utilized Houdini alongside Marvelous Designer. The scene where the turban is pulled off by hand was handled by combining both tools appropriately. The part where the bottom of the turban is grabbed and pulled was created in Houdini, while the natural movement of the scarf underneath was simulated in Marvelous Designer.

Finally, we combined the completed simulation data and character animation data into a single scene, proceeded with rendering, and finished with compositing in After Effects.

# **Min-ji, you have also worked on numerous personal projects, and the expression of wrinkles in your character costumes is exceptionally detailed. Do you have any personal tips for creating realistic wrinkles?**

![89fa3084761849e7b831ce7c3b31bf6d](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202512/80d4961da95048638f075d52a4b7af6b/images/89fa3084761849e7b831ce7c3b31bf6dimgi_515_889f50232584561.689f1e643a07e.png)![bed8ceec182846d78b4d4b20e7275bc0](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202512/80d4961da95048638f075d52a4b7af6b/images/bed8ceec182846d78b4d4b20e7275bc0imgi_146_93ff1b232584561.689f36a3da361-ezgif.com-resize.gif)

I believe the greatest strength of Marvelous Designer lies in its ability to control physical properties in great detail. Therefore, I adjust specific parameters while carefully observing references of the desired fabric and lower the particle distance to capture natural wrinkles that are impossible to recreate by hand.

While it is possible to sculpt wrinkles onto a rough form in ZBrush later, I believe achieving a solid base through Marvelous Designer’s accurate physical calculations results in a much higher level of realism.

![68baf64770d8414eb0d939fcf1346375](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202512/80d4961da95048638f075d52a4b7af6b/images/68baf64770d8414eb0d939fcf1346375imgi_144_fdc0ff232584561.689f2cb4cdd10-ezgif.com-resize.gif)

For neat, tailored clothing, I match the pattern lengths and seam lines exactly. However, to express the feeling of worn clothing or tension around seams, I often deliberately mismatch the lengths of connecting patterns.

![c22c7d3c571a4960a0f393d201b08ecf](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202512/80d4961da95048638f075d52a4b7af6b/images/c22c7d3c571a4960a0f393d201b08ecf%E1%84%8C%E1%85%A1%E1%86%BC%E1%84%80%E1%85%B5%E1%84%92%E1%85%A1_Render.jpg)

![628e23c29db843ee96ee127d10a05c84](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202512/80d4961da95048638f075d52a4b7af6b/images/628e23c29db843ee96ee127d10a05c84%E1%84%8C%E1%85%A1%E1%86%BC%E1%84%80%E1%85%B5%E1%84%92%E1%85%A1_MD_1.png)![542bd063ffd74725a8fb4e5c45cc2075](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202512/80d4961da95048638f075d52a4b7af6b/images/542bd063ffd74725a8fb4e5c45cc2075%E1%84%8C%E1%85%A1%E1%86%BC%E1%84%80%E1%85%B5%E1%84%92%E1%85%A1_MD_2.png)

For example, with the Hanbok and leather jacket I created for the character 'Chang Ki-ha,' I arbitrarily adjusted the pattern lengths of the Hanbok to highlight the aesthetic curves of the fabric folds. I made the sleeves longer than standard to allow for multiple layers of folding, creating richer wrinkles. For the pants, I created a significant difference in pattern lengths to achieve voluminous bunching just above the ankles.

![30ea498ec0f24a579f8c89293ff204db](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202512/80d4961da95048638f075d52a4b7af6b/images/30ea498ec0f24a579f8c89293ff204db%E1%84%8C%E1%85%A1%E1%86%BC%E1%84%80%E1%85%B5%E1%84%92%E1%85%A1_Sp_1.jpg)

Additionally, when a character poses, the volume or shape of the wrinkles sometimes doesn't look right. In such cases, I have occasionally modified the patterns—originally made in an A-pose—to better suit the specific pose. This approach is feasible, of course, because I am working on still images.![8880c505b17740898b75bd876a2ecab9](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202512/80d4961da95048638f075d52a4b7af6b/images/8880c505b17740898b75bd876a2ecab9%E1%84%8C%E1%85%A1%E1%86%BC%E1%84%80%E1%85%B5%E1%84%92%E1%85%A1_Zbr_1.JPG)

Finally, although not shown in these images, when I want to depict stretched or worn-out fabric, I use the Steam tool to locally stretch or shrink areas to artificially generate wrinkles.

# **If you are planning future projects using Marvelous Designer, in what direction would you like to expand your work?**

**Hyun-jong Kim:**  
Lately, I have been studying Blender as well as Cinema 4D, specifically researching workflows that integrate Blender and Marvelous Designer. Since Blender offers excellent compatibility with various other tools compared to Cinema 4D, I expect to find an even more efficient process than my current one.  
In terms of creative work, I am currently working on a light personal project inspired by the game _The Last of Us_ , and I plan to actively utilize Marvelous Designer for this project as well.

**Min-ji Oh:**  
Up until now, I have mostly focused on still images. However, I am currently planning a video project where I utilize Marvelous Designer's simulation features to make costumes flutter naturally in sync with the mood and music.  
While my previous works featured relatively simple clothing, my next project will feature a more flamboyant character. I intend to create an elaborate dress adorned with various decorations to match. I've heard that the latest versions of Marvelous Designer allow for much more detailed control over simulation features, so I am very much looking forward to my next piece!

# [**Hyun-jong Kim(Behance)**](https://www.behance.net/Kinn_hj)

# [**Min-ji Oh(Artstation)**](https://www.artstation.com/ohminji3)

### Community Post Comments:
Comment 1: wow, superB design and animation with audio and graphics.... excellent team work...👏

Comment 2: The animation is so cool😍
content_description: Explore the collaborative artistry of Hyun-jong Kim and Min-ji Oh as they unveil the secrets behind their stunning costume designs inspired by *Dune*, utilizing Marvelous Designer to achieve breathtaking hyper-realism in cloth simulation.
